A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same temperature-modulated open-set recognition research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition experiments, temperature-schedule comparisons, representation visualizations, and training-class ablations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments and expanded schedule, architecture, loss-function, and sensitivity evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v2 retains periodic NegCosSch but expands the proposed method to include a single monotonic negative-cosine increase and linear and exponential increases over training (Section 4.3 and Appendix B). This materially broadens the scheduling procedures. v1's Half-NegCosSch ablation resets the temperature and is not equivalent to the new full-training monotonic schedule.

E1.justification: Reported dataset and task coverage remains CIFAR10, CIFAR+10, CIFAR+50, TinyImageNet, CUB, FGVC-Aircraft, and Stanford Cars, with closed-set classification and open-set recognition. CIFAR evaluations remain in Appendix F.6. The new TinyViT and ProtoCon experiments use existing benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands CE schedule comparisons with controls including random, linear-decrease, logarithmic-increase, and monotonic cosine schedules, and adds a ProtoCon baseline on TinyImageNet. It removes ConOSR comparisons, CE comparisons on CIFAR, and the SSB SupCon+CosSch comparison. The old TinyImageNet step-up and resetting Half-NegCosSch comparisons also disappear. ARPL was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a pretrained TinyViT backbone on CUB, CE without label smoothing and SupCon with label smoothing on TinyImageNet, and a TinyImageNet period comparison using P=100 and P=200. The established benchmark splits, evaluation metrics, CNN configurations, and 600-epoch training regime otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Table 1 systematically tests schedule shape and direction across CE experiments on TinyImageNet and all three SSBs, substantially extending v1's limited alternative-schedule analysis. Appendix F.4 adds period sensitivity tests, and F.2 tests applicability to TinyViT. Existing temperature-range, phase-shift, and training-class-count analyses remain rather than being entirely new.

E5.justification: v1 reports standard deviations across five regular-benchmark splits and error bars for the training-class study. v2 newly specifies five random seeds per split and supplies extensive seed-based standard-deviation tables for its main schedule and loss comparisons (Tables 3–4). Conversely, CIFAR standard deviations disappear from the retained results. The PDFs do not establish an explicit increase from a known previous seed count.

E6.justification: Many SSB values are revised: CUB CE-without-LS accuracy changes from 84.60/86.20 for baseline/periodic NegCosSch in v1 to 84.43/86.30 in v2. Numerous new schedule, TinyViT, ProtoCon, and period-sensitivity results appear, while ConOSR and other comparison results disappear. CIFAR accuracy and AUROC values are retained, with OSCR entries added. These are revised and expanded reported results, not demonstrated same-setting algorithmic gains between versions.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix C add explicit temperature-dependent gradient derivations for negative and positive SupCon pairs and CE, where v1 provided qualitative explanations. New schedule formulas are also defined. These are localized analytical additions; the OSR assumptions remain unchanged, and no new theorem or performance guarantee is established.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion broaden the central contribution from one proposed negative-cosine schedule to a family of effective temperature schedules, explicitly including simple monotonic increases. The retained claims concern improved open- and closed-set recognition without additional computational overhead, particularly on harder semantic-shift benchmarks.

C2.justification: v2 adds a familiarity-hypothesis rationale and explains descending phases and periodic restarts as opportunities to refine instance-specific features and explore nearby solutions. Appendix F.6 adds a ceiling-effect explanation for small CIFAR gains. The earlier limitation concerning few training classes is largely retained there rather than removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds software versions, the ARPL loss weight, and ProtoCon implementation equations. However, v1's explicit project-code URL and statement that code is available are replaced by a future-release promise. The hardware, training-time range, and scheduler code example are largely retained or relocated; the PDFs alone do not establish actual external repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds research connections and citations concerning the familiarity hypothesis, fine-grained OSR, TinyViT, and open-world prompt tuning. Most existing related-work discussion and positioning remain. Kukleva et al.'s updated publication information refers to the same work and is not a new citation.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: temperature effects become a separate section, the method is divided into rationale and schedule choices, and the results emphasize schedule and loss comparisons. Regular-benchmark analyses and limitations move into expanded appendices. The introduction and related work are rewritten, and a reproducibility statement replaces the acknowledgments section.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to include monotonic schedules; the main results tables are extensively restructured into dataset panels and separate loss/schedule columns. New variability, architecture, prototype-loss, and period tables are added. The regular-benchmark plot moves to the appendix with reordered panels, alongside document-wide typography, heading, and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v1 had limited alternative-schedule controls and no uncertainty estimates for its main SSB results. v2's broader schedule comparisons distinguish the benefits of increasing temperature from the particular periodic cosine shape, while Tables 3–4 make variability in the central results assessable. Together with architecture and loss checks, this substantially strengthens the empirical foundation. Removing some comparisons and replacing the available-code link with a future-release promise weakens completeness and reproducibility, but does not outweigh the improved validation.
